Class HttpServer

java.lang.Object
io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.net.http.HttpServer
public final class HttpServer extends Object
A minimal, non-blocking HTTP/1.1 server recognized as compiler intrinsics by Juno, backed by the Arduino WiFiS3 library's WiFiServer on UNO R4 WiFi and by BridgeTCPServer (a listener in arduino-router on Linux) on UNO Q. Requires an active Wifi.begin(String, String) or Wifi.beginAP(String, String) connection. begin(int) serves plain HTTP on every board; beginTls(int, byte[], int, byte[], int) serves HTTPS on the ESP32 boards (Nano ESP32, M5Stack Cardputer), the UNO Q whose MCU runs the TLS session over the bridge, and the Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W.

begin(int) starts listening once. From then on, call accept(byte[], int) once per loop() iteration: it returns immediately with -1 when no client is currently waiting, so the rest of loop() still runs every iteration, or reads a complete request (method, path, and body) within a fixed 5-second deadline once a client has connected. After a successful accept() (a return value of 0 or more), method() and path() report the request that was just read, and exactly one respond call must follow to reply and close that connection before the next accept().

path() is typically matched against known routes with String.equals(Object), e.g. if (HttpServer.path().equals("/status")) .... respond(int, String, String)'s body may be a literal or any runtime String (e.g. a StringBuilder's toString()) — unlike every other intrinsic String parameter in Juno, it is not restricted to a compile-time literal, since a literal's address and a runtime String's pooled address are both just a null-terminated const char* to this method's shim. That runtime String is still bounded by Juno's small runtime-string pool, though; for a body that might not fit, respond(int, String, StringBuilder) instead streams a StringBuilder's current contents directly, with no such cap.

  • Method Details

    • begin

      public static void begin(int port)
      Starts listening on port. Call once, typically right after Wifi.begin(String, String) succeeds.

    • beginTls

      public static boolean beginTls(int port, byte[] certificate, int certificateLength, byte[] privateKey, int privateKeyLength)
      Starts listening for HTTPS on port (usually 443), presenting certificate and proving it with privateKey: both PEM text, typically a self-signed pair read from the SD card, so clients must trust the certificate themselves (e.g. curl --cacert server.crt, or -k). The buffers are parsed here and can be reused afterwards. On success the rest of the API is unchanged: accept(byte[], int) completes the TLS handshake before it reads the request. Returns false when the certificate or key does not parse. ESP32 boards (Nano ESP32, M5Stack Cardputer), UNO Q and Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W only, one connection at a time; call it once, instead of begin(int).

    • accept

      public static int accept(byte[] bodyBuffer, int bodyBufferLength)
      Returns immediately with -1 when no client is currently waiting. Otherwise reads the next request's body into bodyBuffer (truncated to its own length; 0 for a bodyless request such as a plain GET) within a fixed 5-second deadline, and returns the number of body bytes written. Pass bodyBuffer's own array length explicitly, since Juno has no runtime .length for an array method parameter.

    • method

      public static String method()
      The HTTP method ("GET", "POST", ...) of the request from the most recent accept(byte[], int).

    • path

      public static String path()
      The request path (e.g. "/status") of the request from the most recent accept(byte[], int), up to 95 characters; the next accept overwrites it.

    • contentLength

      public static int contentLength()
      The Content-Length header of the request from the most recent accept(byte[], int), or -1 when it had none. It is the size the client declared, so a server can reject a body larger than its buffer (which accept silently truncates) before parsing it.

    • header

      public static int header(String name, byte[] buffer, int bufferLength)
      Copies the value of request header name from the most recent accept(byte[], int) into buffer, truncated to bufferLength, and returns the number of bytes copied, or -1 when the request has no such header. The name is matched case-insensitively and must be a string literal, such as "Mailbox-API-Key"; spaces around the value are trimmed. Only the first 384 bytes of the request's header lines are kept, so a header past that reads as absent.

    • respond

      public static void respond(int status, String contentType, String body)
      Replies with body (a literal or a runtime String), then closes the connection.

    • beginStream

      public static void beginStream(int status, String contentType)
      Starts a response that has no fixed length and keeps the client connected until endStream(), for example multipart/x-mixed-replace video. Send the headers with this call, then write parts with streamBytes(byte[], int) and streamText(String). Served one client at a time, from the same accept(byte[], int) loop. ESP32 boards with the camera capability only (AI Thinker ESP32-CAM).

    • streamBytes

      public static boolean streamBytes(byte[] data, int length)
      Writes the first length bytes of data to the open stream. Returns false once the client has disconnected, so the program can stop producing parts.

    • streamText

      public static boolean streamText(String text)
      Writes text to the open stream. Returns false once the client has disconnected.

    • endStream

      public static void endStream()
      Ends the open stream and closes the client connection.

    • respond

      public static void respond(int status, String contentType, StringBuilder body)
      Replies with body's current contents (built at runtime), then closes the connection.
